C- Reading Comprehension

3) Read the following passage, then answer the questions:


In the heart of the rugged mountains, where the earth bore the scars of countless excavations, tragedy struck the mining community like a thunderbolt from a clear sky Deep within the belly of the earth, a group of dedicated miners toiled tirelessly, their pickaxes echoing in the dimly lit tunnels as they searched for the elusive glimmer of gold.

But as fate would have it, disaster lurked in the shadows of the mine, waiting to unleash its wrath upon the unsuspecting workers. Suddenly, with a deafening roar, the earth trembled and groaned, sending shockwaves through the narrow passages. A section of the mine collapsed, trapping several miners beneath tons of rock and debris.

Amidst the chaos and despair, a frantic rescue operation ensued. Brave souls risked their own lives to dig through the rubble, their hands blistered and bleeding, their hearts heavy with the fear of what they might find beneath the earth's cold embrace.

Hours stretched into eternity as the rescuers fought against time and nature's fury. Finally, a glimmer of hope emerged as they pulled several miners from the wreckage, their faces pale and dust-covered but alive. Cheers erupted from the crowd gathered outside the mine, mingled with tears of relief and gratitude. But amidst the jubilation, a somber reality cast its shadow. Not all who had ventured into the depths of the mine would return to the surface alive. Despite the valiant efforts of the rescue teams, some souls had been claimed by the unforgiving embrace of the earth.

As the sun dipped below the horizon, casting long shadows over the mining town, the community mourned the loss of their fallen comrades. Candlelight vigils flickered in the darkness, illuminating tear-streaked faces as prayers were offered for those who had perished and gratitude for those who had been spared.

Though the scars of the tragedy would linger for years to come, the spirit of resilience burned bright in the hearts of the mining community. They would mourn their losses, but they would also carry on, their determination as unyielding as the mountains that surrounded them.

questions.passage:
Read the following passage, then answer the questions:

The environment is a hot topic of discussion these days. To save the planet Earth, all nations are coming to an accord. Through our negative feelings and emotions, we damage not only the soil and the water, but also the subtle environment. We are now victims of our own needs and greed. Our minds are not within our control. We spend a lot of time listening to stories about other people in life, but we hardly ever hear about ourselves. How should we care for our minds? How can one live in the here and now? How can one be thankful and joyful? We haven't learned this yet. The most regrettable thing is this. What then is the solution? This is where we are reminded of a very fundamental principle that governs our environment, our mind, our emotions and our life in general.

Currently positivity lies at the core of our being, our body can withstand the vibration of happiness and tranquility for a far longer period of time than it can negative emotions. Similar to how protons and neutrons make up the center of an atom and electrons only make up the perimeter, so too are bliss, positivity, and joy the center of our existence, surrounded as it is by a cloud of negative ions. We may quickly and easily overcome our negative feelings with the aid of breathing. We are able to remove this cloud of negativity by practicing meditation and specific breathing exercises.

You have so much to gain from this life. Once you take some time off, you'll notice that your soul is rejuvenated. Your grin is what your soul is aching for. If you could provide this, you would feel invigorated throughout the entire year and nothing could ever make you unhappy. Everybody aspires to lead prosperous lives. However, you want to succeed even if you have no idea what it is. What signifies success? Is being wealthy alone a sign of success? Why do you think success is correlated with money? Because having money allows you to be free to do as you like. Even though you have a sizable money account, you might need to have bypass surgery because of your ulcers and stomachaches. ; can't eat this, can't do this, can't do that. We expend half our health to gain wealth and then spend half our wealth to gain back the lost health. Is this success? In fact, it is very bad mathematics.
